fixes.title: Fix RESTPECT typo and add vfmlaq ISA guard
fixes.problem: Two bugs in mul-mat-dispatch.cpp: (1) GGML_RESTPECT typo causes compile error on strict compilers, (2) vfmlaq_f32 requires ARMv8.1-A FCMA feature but has no guard — will SIGILL on Cortex-A53/A72.

fixes.title: Implement calibrate_model() orchestrator with llama_decode integration
fixes.problem: calibrate_model() is declared in calibrator.h but has no implementation file. The calibration algorithms (kl_entropy, aciq, eq_refine) are implemented, but there is no code that (1) loads a model, (2) runs llama_decode() with calibration text, (3) collects intermediate activations, (4) feeds them to the calibration algorithms. llama-calibrate binary is not built.
fixes.impact: Calibration suite cannot be used end-to-end. The KL/ACIQ/EQ algorithms work standalone but have no integration with llama.cpp's forward pass.

implementation_plan: 1. Load model: llama_model_load(model_path) + llama_init_from_model()
2. Parse calibration_data: read text file, one sample per line
3. For each sample (up to config.n_calibration_samples):
a. Tokenize: llama_tokenize(vocab, sample, tokens, ...)
b. Create batch: llama_batch_init(n_tokens, n_embd, 1)
c. Decode: llama_decode(ctx, batch)
d. Extract activations per layer via ggml graph interception:
- Set a callback on each matmul input tensor
- Record absmax + histogram per tensor name
e. If calibrate_kv_cache: also collect KV tensor values from llama_kv_cache
4. After all samples: compute scales using config.method
- KL_ENTROPY: call compute_kl_threshold() per tensor
- ACIQ: call compute_aciq_scale() per tensor
- EQ_REFINE: seed from KL, then call refine_layer_scale() per layer
5. Write scale table: write_scale_table(output_table_path, entries)
6. Return 0 on success
Integration challenge: step 3d requires either:
(a) A ggml graph callback API to intercept intermediate tensors, OR
(b) A custom llama_context hook that copies activations after each layer, OR
(c) Replacing the model's forward graph with an instrumented version

Approach (b) is simplest: add a callback to llama_context that fires after each transformer layer, providing access to the activation tensors. The imatrix collection in llama.cpp already uses a similar mechanism (cb_eval).
1. Read scale table: read_scale_table(table_path) → map<tensor_name, scales>
2. Load GGUF model: llama_model_load(model_path)
3. For each weight tensor:
a. Look up scale by tensor name in the table
b. If found: pass scale to ggml_quantize_chunk() (same path as imatrix)
c. If missing: use default absmax quantization
4. Write output GGUF: standard llama-quantize output path
Note: llama-quantize already accepts an imatrix parameter. The scale table
plugs into the same code path — pass it as the imatrix argument to
llama_model_quantize(). The per-channel scales are interpreted as
importance weights that guide the quantization thresholds.

changes.replace:
add_executable(llama-calibrate
    calibrator.cpp
    quantize_with_scales.cpp
    kl_entropy.cpp
    aciq.cpp
    eq_refine.cpp
    scale_table.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(llama-calibrate PRIVATE llama llama-common)
install(TARGETS llama-calibrate RUNTIME DESTINATION bin)
changes.note: If the CMakeLists.txt already has this target commented out, uncomment it. Otherwise add it.

validation: build/bin/llama-calibrate --model <test.gguf> --method aciq --calibrate <data.txt> --output test.table produces non-empty table
fixes.note: This is the largest fix — requires new implementation files. The calibration algorithms themselves are done; this is purely the integration glue. The cb_eval callback approach from llama.cpp's imatrix tooling is the reference pattern.

fixes.title: Add Q4_K shader full implementation (6-bit scale unpacking)
fixes.problem: gemm_q4_k.comp is a scaffold — the Q4_K super-block structure uses 6-bit packed scales that need bit manipulation to unpack. The shader has placeholder comments instead of the actual dequant math.
fixes.impact: Q4_K (the most popular weight quant type) has no working iGPU shader. Q4_0 and Q8_0 shaders are production-ready.

files.implementation_detail:
Q4_K block (144 bytes per 256 weights):
  - d (2B fp16): super-block scale
  - dmin (2B fp16): super-block min scale  
  - scales (12B): 8x 6-bit packed scales (Llama.cpp 6-bit encoding)
  - qs (128B): 256 nibbles packed 2-per-byte

The 6-bit scale encoding packs 8 scales into 12 bytes:
  scales[0] = (s[0] & 0x3F)
  scales[1] = ((s[0] >> 6) | (s[1] << 2)) & 0x3F
  scales[2] = ((s[1] >> 4) | (s[2] << 4)) & 0x3F
  scales[3] = ((s[2] >> 2)) & 0x3F
  (repeat for scales 4-7 using s[3..5])
  scales[4] = (s[6] & 0x3F) | ((s[8] & 0x0F) << 6)
  ...

In GLSL, read from uint[] SSBO and extract bytes via bit-shift.

The shader should:
1. Load the super-block scale d and dmin
2. Unpack the 8 6-bit sub-block scales
3. For each sub-block (32 weights): dequant w = d * sub_scale * (q - 8) - dmin * sub_min
4. Subgroup cooperative dot product as in Q4_0 shader

validation: Q4_K GEMM output matches CPU reference within fp32 epsilon
fixes.note: Lower priority — Q4_0 and Q8_0 shaders are production-ready and cover most use cases. Q4_K can be added later.
